canonical_title: In Pursuit of VALIS: Selections from the Exegesis
author: Philip K. Dick (edited by Lawrence Sutin)
card_summary: Lawrence Sutin's 1991 Underwood-Miller anthology, the first substantial published gathering from Dick's Exegesis, arranging excerpts thematically to make the vast private journal readable.
page_summary:
Published in 1991 by Underwood-Miller of Novato, California, and edited by Lawrence Sutin, In Pursuit of VALIS was the first serious attempt to bring the Exegesis before general readers. Sutin selected from the roughly eight thousand handwritten and typed pages Dick produced between 1974 and his death in 1982, then organized the fragments by theme rather than chronology so that Dick's recurring preoccupations, God, time, cosmology, salvation, madness, could be followed as lines of thought.

The result is a curated distillation rather than a complete text: a fraction of the whole, shaped by an editor's judgment about what was coherent and representative. For two decades, until the 2011 Jackson and Lethem edition appeared, this volume was the primary way scholars and readers encountered the Exegesis at all.

The portal preserves two manifestations of the anthology, the longer running over three hundred pages. Researchers can read it against the portal's full Exegesis materials at /exegesis to see how Sutin's selections relate to the larger manuscript.
